_comment: v0.16 I1 giver (#306, ruling 1). Three route arms converge on `handover`, which carries the only grant, so the reward cannot double-fire. Every gated node keeps an ungated exit.

commission.speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
commission.text: I have been sitting in a paper shop for an hour. On this street it is the one room where a woman may hold something closed and nobody asks her to open it. I have needed the hour.

text_variants.text: You went, then. Sit down and tell me what he said. Every word, please. I have had forty years of the polite half.
It sits differently on the chain. I noticed before I looked. You were paid for the silver. Thank you for the remainder.

text_variants._comment: #318. Every v0.18 variant gates on a counter no shipped fixture holds, so the pinned I1 canonicals can never match one (the text_variants-vs-pinned-base trap).
text_variants.text: I have not put the card down since it came and I have not answered it either. Both of those are being noticed by somebody, I expect.
A clerk with a good hand and a rented block. Forty years of keeping very still, and it was a man renting my mother's initials by the hour to people who wanted a door opened.
I answered it in my own hand. Two lines and no apology in either of them. That is the first thing I have signed in eleven years that nobody had to be told about afterwards.

options.text: "He'll set it. He wanted the true thing said first, and it's said."
"I stood at his bench while he laid the ward. It's set properly."
"Your mother's stone was real. I have it back."

options._comment: #318 entry. Gated on the I1 terminal, so no shipped canonical can render this row and every pinned option array here holds.
options.text: "You've been holding that card since I came in."
"I have the hand that did it."

the_card.speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
the_card.text: It came to my rooms before breakfast. Cream, no crest on it, one line, in a hand I have seen twice in my life on paper I was not supposed to be holding either time. It asks me to confirm a signature.

the_hand.speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
the_hand.text: I have signed nothing of consequence since the year my mother died. I am not going to say whose hand it is in a shop with a scribe in it. You already know which house I mean, because I told you where this city is run from and you did not laugh at me. She does not write to people like me. She writes about them, and only once something with her attention on it has started to move.

options.text: "So somebody's been signing with your name."

terms_card.speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
terms_card._comment: The thread's premise, in her own voice: the second of the two assets her shipped `terms` node names is the one being spent.
terms_card.text: Somebody has, and it has been out in this city doing business without me for long enough that a woman who notices everything has noticed. I will not answer that card until I can say who. Start at the counter of this very shop. There is a scribe there who rents a blank seal by the hour and who has never once asked me how I am.

the_name.speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
the_name.text: A rented block and a good hand. I am not angry at him. I used up angry on larger people, forty years of them, and he is very small. Take the block off whatever table it is sitting on and I will answer the card myself, in my own hand, which is a thing I have been putting off doing for a very long time.

after.speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
after.text: She has not replied. She will not. That is not how any of it works and I would not have the first idea what to do with a reply if one came. What I have instead is a card in a drawer with my own name on the back of it, and the strange discovery that I would rather be noticed than left alone.

after_two.speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
after_two.text: Three, then. Do not tell me the third one is the ring. I would have to be gracious about it and I have used all of that up this week.

the_stone.speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
the_stone._comment: Nobility layer (controller amendment A1): her only acknowledgment of who really owns this city, oblique and Vol-1-safe. Never name her own house.
the_stone.text: My mother's. The stone in it is glass. I have known since I was nineteen and I have never once said so out loud, and I am not going to begin by saying it to a jeweller who will write it on an order. This city is run from a house you cannot see from any street in it, by a woman who notices everything worth noticing. A glass stone is exactly the right size to stay beneath that notice. I intend to keep it there.

options.text: "Then why have it set at all?"

why_keep.speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
why_keep.text: Because she wore it to every hard thing she ever did and it never once let her down. The stone was glass for all forty of those years. It did not matter then and I will not let it start mattering now. I want the setting held properly. The stone can stay glass.

terms.speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
terms.text: There is an enchanter with a bench in the alleys who will not touch a piece until somebody in the transaction tells him the truth about it. He is right to insist and I cannot be the one who does it. Twenty five gold when it is set. Do not be charming at him. My house has exactly two assets left: its name, and the habit people have of not looking past it. Tell him the truth of the stone and keep the name out of his order book.

handover.speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
handover.text: Then it is done, and done in the open, which I did not expect and did not know I wanted. Here. My mother had a second piece, plain, honest, worth a tenth of the first and worn twice as often. I would rather it went to somebody who earned it. It has spent long enough in the box.

options.text: "Keep it. I don't need paying for this."
